title: Systems of coherent modules on the thickenings X_n are coherent formal modules on X
statement: Let $A$ be a Noetherian ring [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring], $I\subseteq A$ an ideal, $S=\operatorname{Spec}A$, $S_n=\operatorname{Spec}(A/I^{n+1})$ ($n\ge0$), $X\to S$ a morphism of finite type [def-weil-finite-type-morphism], $X_n=X\times_SS_n$ [def-pc-base-change] with the closed immersions $j_n:X_n\to X$ and $i_n:X_n\to X_{n+1}$ ($j_{n+1}i_n=j_n$), and $\mathcal I=I\mathcal O_X$ the quasi-coherent ideal sheaf generated by $I$. Then: (1) $X$ is Noetherian and $j_n$ is a closed immersion [def-weil-closed-immersion] with ideal sheaf $\mathcal I^{n+1}$ [def-sbc-closed-immersion-ideal-sheaf]. (2) Let $\mathrm{Sys}$ be the category of systems $(\mathcal F_n,\varphi_n)_{n\ge0}$ of coherent $\mathcal O_{X_n}$-modules $\mathcal F_n$ [pqf-def-coherent] and isomorphisms $\varphi_n:i_n^*\mathcal F_{n+1}\to\mathcal F_n$ [def-pc-module-pullback], a morphism $(\mathcal F_n,\varphi_n)\to(\mathcal G_n,\varphi'_n)$ being a family of $\mathcal O_{X_n}$-linear $u_n:\mathcal F_n\to\mathcal G_n$ with $u_n\circ\varphi_n=\varphi'_n\circ i_n^*u_{n+1}$. The functor sending $(\mathcal F_n,\varphi_n)$ to the inverse system $(j_{n-1,*}\mathcal F_{n-1})_{n\ge1}$, whose transition map $j_{n,*}\mathcal F_n\to j_{n,*}i_{n-1,*}\mathcal F_{n-1}=j_{n-1,*}\mathcal F_{n-1}$ is $j_{n,*}$ of the map $\mathcal F_n\to i_{n-1,*}\mathcal F_{n-1}$ adjoint to $\varphi_{n-1}$, is an equivalence of categories $\mathrm{Sys}\to\mathit{Coh}(X,\mathcal I)$ [def-weil-pbc-coherent-formal-module]. (3) For a coherent $\mathcal O_X$-module $\mathcal F$, the system $(\mathcal F|_{X_n},c_n)$, $\mathcal F|_{X_n}=j_n^*\mathcal F$ and $c_n:i_n^*(\mathcal F|_{X_{n+1}})\cong\mathcal F|_{X_n}$ the canonical isomorphisms, is sent to an object isomorphic to $\mathcal F^\wedge$, by the isomorphisms $j_{n,*}j_n^*\mathcal F\cong\mathcal F/\mathcal I^{n+1}\mathcal F$, naturally in $\mathcal F$; hence for coherent $\mathcal F,\mathcal G$ the families $(u_n:\mathcal G|_{X_n}\to\mathcal F|_{X_n})_{n\ge0}$ with $u_n\circ c_n=c_n\circ i_n^*u_{n+1}$ correspond bijectively to the morphisms $\mathcal G^\wedge\to\mathcal F^\wedge$ of $\mathit{Coh}(X,\mathcal I)$, the family $(u|_{X_n})_n$ of an $\mathcal O_X$-linear $u:\mathcal G\to\mathcal F$ corresponding to $u^\wedge$, and an isomorphism $\mathcal F^\wedge\cong(j_{n-1,*}\mathcal F_{n-1})_n$ in $\mathit{Coh}(X,\mathcal I)$ corresponds to isomorphisms $\psi_n:\mathcal F|_{X_n}\to\mathcal F_n$ with $\varphi_n\circ i_n^*\psi_{n+1}=\psi_n\circ c_n$. (4) For a coherent $\mathcal O_{X_0}$-module $\mathcal F_0$ one has $\operatorname{Supp}(j_{0,*}\mathcal F_0)=j_0(\operatorname{Supp}\mathcal F_0)$, and $\operatorname{Supp}(\mathcal F_0)$ is proper over $S_0$ (for $X_0\to S_0$) if and only if $j_0(\operatorname{Supp}\mathcal F_0)$ is proper over $S$ (for $X\to S$) [def-weil-pbc-closed-subset-proper-over-base]; so the equivalence of (2) identifies the systems with $\operatorname{Supp}(\mathcal F_0)$ proper over $S_0$ with $\mathit{Coh}_{\text{support proper over }S}(X,\mathcal I)$.
